text:
Fifteen games is a long time to go without leaving the building empty-handed. Minnesota's run of points ended Wednesday night in a 4-3 loss to Utah, and Kirill Kaprizov's personal 15-game point streak went with it. Michael Russo of The Athletic called it a rare sloppy effort, and the box score backs him up: the Wild's top line was shut out, Joel Eriksson Ek took four minors, and the power play went 1 for 6.

That last number is the one that will sting. With 3:45 left and the Wild down a goal, Barrett Hayton high-sticked Eriksson Ek off a faceoff and Minnesota got four straight minutes of power play, per Heather Rule of NHL.com. They could not find the tying goal. The closest they came was Maxim Shabanov in the final minute, stopped by Karel Vejmelka on the most valuable save of the night.

The game turned in a wild middle period. Lawson Crouse had given Utah a first-period lead, and Logan Cooley made it 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Bobby Brink answered on a Wild power play, Dmitri Simashev restored the two-goal lead 44 seconds later on a 2% chance, the least likely goal of the night, and Blake Coleman cut it back to one. Dylan Guenther scored with 49 seconds left in the period, off Cooley and Anders Lee, and that goal pushed Utah's win chance from 72% to 88%. Coleman scored again with 4:04 left, his second of the night, but it only set up the frustration of that long power play.

By our replays of every shot, this was close to a coin flip: Minnesota deserved to win 54% of the time, and the two teams combined for barely four expected goals. The difference was in net. Jesper Wallstedt allowed four goals on 20 shots, about two more than the chances deserved. Utah, meanwhile, earned a split with the Wild after losing 3-1 to them in October, and Cooley and Guenther, two picks from the Coyotes era, look like the core of something.
headline: Mammoth end the Wild's 15-game point streak
